---
title: "7 · Time Series: Dynamical Systems, Chaos and Embedding"
code-tools: false
toc: false
---

A forecast maps the past of a signal to a value at a chosen horizon, and we score it by the capacity, the squared correlation between forecast and target. We describe dynamical systems by their state, phase space, flow map and attractors, follow the volume of a set of states with Liouville's theorem, and introduce three benchmark signals, the Lorenz-63 model, the Mackey–Glass delay equation at three delays and the Santa Fe laser record. Small errors grow at the rate of the Lyapunov exponents, which set a fundamental limit on the prediction horizon, and the Kaplan–Yorke dimension measures how many dimensions the attractor really occupies. Takens' theorem says that a window of past values carries the full state, so that a forecast map exists, and we choose its delay by the mutual information and its dimension by false nearest neighbours. The lecture ends with the characteristics of the benchmark signals, everything a forecast from the record alone needs.
